work.text: Authentic pictures by Ni Tsan are not very common; yet, a dozen or more are known in public and private collections in China and Japan, most of them representing autumn views with stretches of quiet water between rocky shores with a few bare trees.

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: A History of Early Chinese Painting, vol. II

work.text: The cool greyish atmosphere is perfectly suggested by the tone of the paper and the light ink; they seem to be ensouled by the quiet resignation of the autumn day.

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: A History of Early Chinese Painting, vol. II

moment.text: the restrained thinness of Ni Zan and the almost embroidered richness of Wang Meng distinguished their work from that of their immediate predecessors.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors
source.title: Four Masters of the Yuan dynasty

moment.text: Nothing could be further from the warm, sensuous, energetic art of Wang Meng than the icy restraint of Ni Tsan
